newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ says high fuel prices may prompt fare hike.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ says high fuel prices may prompt fare hike.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd chairman Bob Matthew said on Wednesday that should recent high jet fuel prices continue to prevail in 1997, the industry would have to raise air fares to recover costs.

Matthew said in the last financial year outbound traffic increased by 17 percent on the previous year, which "while a positive for us, does not fully compensate for the substantially lower inbound traffic growth presently being experienced".
Matthew said a negative implication from the stronger New Zealand dollar was the reduced revenue receipts on conversion of foreign currency sales.
"Again, while this is partially compensated by lower New Zealand dollar charges for costs incurred overseas, the net effect is reduced yields and margins," he said.
Matthew said Air NZ would not add any new aircraft to the international fleet this year and only a modest expansion was planned for the following year.
"This is a time to do all we can to improve passenger load factors, yields and margins. Much attention is already being focused on this area and positive results are emerging progressively," he said.
Matthew hinted at possible outsourcing of some business areas, but did not give details.

"There may well be some things that we should not continue to do ourselves becase they are not fundamental to the company's core airline business and can more effectively be obtained from others," he said.
Matthew said it would be premature to provide an explicit forecast for the current year.
He said the year to June 1998 would be one where the company, which recently acquired a half share in in Australia's Ansett Airways, benefited substantially from the initiatives already taken.
He said Air NZ was close to concluding comprehensive comemrcial alliance agremeents with other leading international airlines.

"These major developments are expected to deliver substantial benefits to the company, though it will be six months or so before the major financial benefits from these arrangements start to come to account," he said.
